item.title: Savannah Guthrie posts message to her mother's kidnapper asking to provide proof she is alive
item.description: NBC “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie sent a public message to her 84-year-old mother’s kidnapper on Wednesday saying that her family is ready to talk but wants proof that she is alive.

item.title: Bryant University students get big game experience at Radio Row
item.description: The Super Bowl brings thousands of members of the media to the host city, and many of them set up shop at Radio Row. Among them this year is a group of 10 Bryant University students who were able to secure a table thanks to their professor, former Patriots tight end and Super Bowl champion Christian Fauria.

item.title: Woman accused of stealing $30K in merchandise from New England retailers
item.description: A Cranston woman accused of stealing thousands of dollars worth of merchandise from retailers across New England was arrested last week.

item.title: In Providence, January snowstorm cleanup cost tops $562K and climbing
item.description: Providence has spent approximately $562,660 on snow cleanup costs from the Jan. 25-26 storm as of Tuesday, but there are still outstanding expenses.

item.title: Verdict tossed in 1999 Providence cold case after court error
item.description: A judge has ordered a new trial for a man previously convicted in the strangling death of a woman behind a Providence middle school nearly 30 years ago.

item.title: RIDOT removed over 700 bridges from its count, then said it met repair goal
item.description: The agency changed its math in recent months, pushing it past the 90% target for bridge condition set 10 years ago.

item.title: Peter Alviti resigning as RIDOT director; McKee plans nationwide search
item.description: Alviti, who has led the department for a decade, came under withering criticism over the Washington Bridge crisis.
